patch_description: Replaces the sliding polynomial fit with a bidirectional constant-velocity Kalman smoother whose process noise Q is adapted per-sample from local second differences, using quadrature noise subtraction (local d2 energy minus the noise-only 6σ_r² floor) clipped to a tuned floor (0.05σ_r) and cap (0.6σ_r). This shrinks Q where dynamics are indistinguishable from noise (fewer slope changes and false reversals) while still trusting genuine accelerations (low lag). The fused estimate then passes through zero-lag bidirectional one-pole smoothers (phase delay cancelled by the mirrored pass) and a noise-scaled slope deadzone that flattens sub-noise steps without touching real moves. The result targets the weakest metrics — smoothness/slope-change count — while retaining the accuracy and responsiveness of the Kalman trend estimate. Interface, output length convention, and slicing contract are unchanged.
